family.construction: Take k renamed copies of the R44AS maxdef-critical parent. Keep each block's five nonpivot variables disjoint and identify all local pivots into one shared global pivot x.
family.siblings: After x=0 or x=1, the siblings are variable-disjoint unions of k copies of the two base R44AS siblings A and B, respectively, each with maxdef k.

fixed_deviation_lower_bound.setup: Let phi be any signed literal substitution transport in either sibling direction and let S={v:phi(v)!=v} be its deviation support.
argument: If a target block contains no variable of S, then phi is identity on every variable of that block.
All source clauses are confined to source blocks with pairwise disjoint variable sets.
Therefore every clause of that untouched target block can only be witnessed by a clause in the same-labeled source block.
This would give an identity local transport between the two base R44AS siblings.
Exact R44BQ-K5 replay excludes identity transport in both directions on the base pair.
Hence every target block intersects S.
fixed_deviation_lower_bound.conclusion: |S|>=k for every valid deviation-form substitution transport in either direction.

existence_of_unbounded_transport.construction: Apply the R44BP signed-permutation transport independently in each block. Signed permutations are a special case of R44BS substitutions.
existence_of_unbounded_transport.meaning: The relation class itself remains applicable; only every universal fixed deviation bound fails.

theorem_effect.claim: For every fixed constant K there exists k>K such that G_k is maxdef-critical and its sibling pair admits a substitution transport but no valid substitution transport with deviation support <=K.

next_exact_question: Can unbounded-support substitution transports be discovered in polynomial time on maxdef-critical siblings by exploiting block/global structure, or can critical-only discovery be proved hard? Fixed-K enumeration is now formally exhausted as a universal route.
